summary: Ludwig Diestel was a religious studies scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1845–1848). He held posts at the universities of Greifswald (~1858–1862), Bonn (~1862–1867), Jena (~1867–1872), and Tübingen (~1872–1879).

Ludwig Heller, an Indologist and linguist, studied under Franz Kielhorn and earned a doctorate at Göttingen and a habilitation at Greifswald. He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin and Greifswald before serving at the University of Tartu in 1918.

Ludwig Lange studied under Theodor Benfey at Leipzig and earned his habilitation at Göttingen. A scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology, he held professorships at Charles University, the University of Giessen, and the University of Leipzig, serving as Leipzig's Rektor.

Ludwig Ross was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Kiel University (~1825–1829). He held academic posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859).

Ludwig Wittgenstein studied at TH Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge/Trinity College, earning a Ph.D. A philosopher, he served as a lecturer, fellow, and professor of philosophy at Cambridge and Trinity College between 1929 and 1947.
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He held a post as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

Luigi Suali was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bologna (~1899–1904) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1904–1906), later holding a post at the University of Pavia (~1907–1951).

Luis Oscar Gómez studied at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale University under Stanley Insler, and the University of Michigan. In Indology and Buddhist studies, he was a long-time professor and department chair at Michigan and directed the Mangalam Research Center.

Luise Hercus studied at St Anne's College and the Australian National University. Working in Indology and linguistics, she held posts at St Anne's College (1948–1954), the University of Adelaide (1965–1969), and the Australian National University (~1969–1991).
Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at Sherubtse College, Government Law College, Mumbai, and the University of Edinburgh.

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima, a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot beginning in 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Lutz Bieg studied at Heidelberg University and Freie Universität Berlin. A sinologist, he served as professor of China, modern Chinese literature, and Chinese philosophy at the University of Cologne from 1989 to 2008.

Lynn Struve studied at the University of Washington (~1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (~1967–1976). A scholar of sinology and history/archaeology, she held a faculty post at Indiana University Bloomington (~1977–2011).

Lynn Thomas, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, earned degrees from Lancaster University and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford (-1987). She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer studied under Étienne Marc Quatremère and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. Working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at INALCO, Collège de France, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Léon Vandermeersch studied at INALCO, Paris Diderot, EPHE, and the University of Paris. A sinologist and philosopher, he held posts at the National Museum of Vietnamese History, Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and EFEO.

Lê Mạnh Thát studied at Saigon University (~1962–1965) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1974). A scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history/archaeology, he held a post at Vạn Hạnh University (~1974–1975).

M. A. Mehendale, an Indologist and linguist, served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and held a professorship at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983, 2026).
M. Athar Ali was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1948 to 1961 and served there as a historian from ~1953 to 1995.
